elements.quote: This systematic review assesses the scientific evidence regarding the effectiveness of organisational-level workplace mental health interventions on stress, burnout, non-clinical depressive and anxiety symptoms, and wellbeing in construction workers.

Outcomes were stress, burnout and non-clinical depression and anxiety symptoms, and wellbeing (primary) and workplace changes and sickness absenteeism (secondary).

elements.quote: The specific review questions are: (1) Are organisational-level mental health programmes effective in reducing stress, burnout, non-clinical depressive and anxiety symptoms, and in enhancing mental wellbeing in construction workers? (2) Are organisational-level mental health programmes effective in reducing stress, burnout, non-clinical depressive and anxiety symptoms and in enhancing mental wellbeing in SME construction workers?
elements.reason: Review questions are explicitly stated in a clear, question-based format.
No evidence found stating planned comparisons using PICO or an appropriate variant in the retrieved evidence.
The complete search strategy is referenced but not provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: included studies published in English between January 2010 and May 2022 to reflect intervention efforts in the modern construction workplace.
elements.reason: Search limits are described and justified by reference to eligibility criteria.

elements.reason: PRESS is cited, but adaptations are not described.

elements.quote: Primary outcomes included quantitative measurements of aspects of mental health and wellbeing, secondary outcomes included organisational outcomes such as absenteeism, especially if linked to health issues, and changes to the psychosocial work environment.
elements.reason: Outcomes are listed and partially defined, but some definitions (e.g., mental health and wellbeing) are implicit or lack detail.
No specification of time frame for each outcome domain is provided in the evidence.
No explicit statement on whether all compatible results within each outcome domain were sought.

elements.quote: Reported outcomes, that were not specified as primary or secondary outcomes for the purpose of this review were not included in the results table nor the synthesis.
elements.reason: Process for selecting results is described indirectly for synthesis, implying only primary and secondary outcomes were considered, but not explicitly for data collection.
No changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance are reported.
No changes to processes for selecting results within eligible outcome domains are reported.

elements.quote: Primary outcomes included quantitative measurements of aspects of mental health and wellbeing, secondary outcomes included organisational outcomes such as absenteeism, especially if linked to health issues, and changes to the psychosocial work environment. As organisational-level interventions target the psychosocial work environment, these changes were deemed important intermediary effects of mental health promotion. Absenteeism was deemed as a general organisational outcome measure, that is sensitive to short-term and long-term mental health effects...
elements.reason: Primary and secondary outcomes are specified with rationales for their importance.

elements.quote: Mean differences (pre- and post- intervention) with p-values were reported and adjusted regression coefficients or adjusted Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals, if available, were tabulated, brought together, and summarized using narrative synthesis.
elements.reason: Specifies effect measures such as mean differences, adjusted regression coefficients, and adjusted odds ratios used in the narrative synthesis for outcomes.
No evidence of thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect size and their rationale reported in the retrieved evidence.
No evidence of methods to re-express synthesized results using another effect measure described in the retrieved evidence.
No evidence of justification for the choice of effect measure reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The classification developed in a systematic review on organisational-level wellbeing interventions by Fox et al [63] was applied to the narrative synthesis of studies using four categories: scheduling interventions, job and task modification, relational and team dynamics interventions and participatory process interventions. In addition, the Integrated Workplace Mental Health Intervention approach [57,58] served as a framework for synthesis and summary according to (a) interventions for the promotion of mental wellbeing and (b) interventions for the protection of mental health problems.
elements.reason: The review explicitly describes processes for deciding study eligibility for each synthesis by applying classification frameworks based on intervention characteristics, aligning with the requirement.

elements.quote: Mean differences (pre- and post- intervention) with p-values were reported and adjusted regression coefficients or adjusted Odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals, if available, were tabulated, brought together, and summarized using narrative synthesis.

elements.quote: The narrative synthesis was guided by the aim to identify which types of interventions were effective or not effective to positively promote mental health and wellbeing and to protect mental health in the construction sector. In the evidence synthesis, we considered the magnitude of effect found in each study and the methodological quality of the study as rated by the QATQS global score for each study.
elements.reason: Methods for synthesis include considering effect size and study quality, which can explore heterogeneity, but not explicitly stated as for exploring causes of heterogeneity.

elements.quote: Atotal of 1326 records were identified from five databases. An additional 35 records were identified through the citation chaining of records included in the full-text review. Following removal of duplicates, the title and abstract of 1129 records were reviewed for eligibility. 1090 records were excluded
elements.reason: Numbers for records identified (1326 + 35), screened (1129), and excluded after initial screening (1090) are reported, but the number of duplicates removed before screening is not explicitly stated.

elements.quote: the full text was reviewed for 39 articles. Primary reasons for exclusion at full-text review were ineligible outcomes (n = 14) and ineligible study design (n = 10).
elements.reason: Number assessed for eligibility (39) and primary reasons for exclusion with numbers are reported, but the number of reports sought and not retrieved is not reported.

elements.quote: five articles from four studies were identified as eligible for inclusion in the review
